title: The Tale of the Enchanted King

paragraphs.en: My father, King Mahmud of the Black Islands, ruled for seventy years before I succeeded him at age twenty-five. My cousin, who loved me deeply, refused to eat or drink if I was away even for a day. We lived together for five years until one evening.
paragraphs.zh: 我的父亲，黑岛国王玛姆德，在位七十年后，我才在二十五岁那年继承了王位。我的堂弟妹对我情深意重，只要我离开哪怕一天，她就绝食绝水。我们一起生活了五年，直到一个傍晚。

paragraphs.en: That night, I lay down in this very spot and ordered two maids to fan me while the cook prepared a meal. As I lay there uneasily, unable to sleep, I overheard the maid at my head say to her companion: "What a pity for our poor master with such a damned mistress, and him so young!" The other replied, "May God damn all treacherous women.
paragraphs.zh: 那个晚上，我躺在这个位置，吩咐两个女仆为我扇风，而厨师则在准备晚餐。我辗转反侧，难以入眠，无意中听到头边的女仆对同伴说：“可怜我们那位倒霉的主人，还得忍受这么一个可恶的情妇，而且他还那么年轻！”另一人回应道，“但愿上帝诅咒所有背信弃义的女人。”

paragraphs.en: Such a young man like our master should not live with this woman who spends every night out." Mas'uda added, "Is our master stupid? When he wakes at night, doesn't he find her gone?"
paragraphs.zh: 像我们主人这样年轻的人，不应该和这个每晚都外出的女人一起生活。“马苏达补充道，“难道我们的主人这么笨吗？每当夜半醒来，他不发现她早已不在了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Her companion responded, "Alas, may God trip the bitch our mistress. She leaves him drugged and asleep until dawn, then returns to stay out all night. What a pity!"
paragraphs.zh: 她的同伴叹了口气，说道：“唉，但愿老天爷让那贱妇摔个跟头。她让他昏睡到天亮，自己却整夜在外。真是可惜！”

paragraphs.en: My lord, upon hearing the maids' conversation, I was furious and eagerly awaited nightfall. When my wife returned from her bath, we ate little at our meal and retired early. Pretending to drink from a cup, I poured its contents out and went to bed.
paragraphs.zh: 主上，听闻侍女们的谈话后，我气得几乎要爆炸，迫不及待地等着夜幕降临。当夫人从沐浴中归来时，我们连饭都吃得很少，便早早地上床休息了。我假装在喝酒，其实却将杯中的酒倒掉了，然后径自躺下。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I lay down, she said, "Sleep forever, for your sight disgusts me and your company bores me." She then dressed herself, perfumed with incense, took my sword, and left the room.
paragraphs.zh: 一躺下，她便说道：“你去永远沉睡吧，你的相貌让我作呕，你的陪伴令我厌烦。”说完，她📐自己，焚香沐浴后，拿起我的剑，离开了房间。

paragraphs.en: Morning came before Shahrazad could continue her story, leaving Dinarzad intrigued. Dinarzad asked her sister to tell a tale that night, promising it would be delightful. Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，沙赫拉兹德还没来得及继续她的故事，就不得不中断。迪纳兹达被故事深深吸引，央求姐姐当晚再给她讲一个，保证会非常精彩。沙赫拉兹德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: The enchanted young man told the king: After his wife left the palace, I followed her through the city until she reached the gate. She spoke words I couldn't understand, and the gate opened by itself. We entered a hut made of palm leaves, leading to a domed structure built from sun-dried bricks.
paragraphs.zh: 那位施了魔法的年轻人对国王说：“自从我妻子离开宫殿后，我一直跟着她穿过了整个城市，直到她来到城门。她说了些我不懂的话，城门竟然自动开了。我们走进了一间用棕榈叶搭建的小屋，里面是一个用晒干砖块建成的穹顶建筑。”

paragraphs.en: Inside, my wife knelt before an old black man sitting on reed shavings in tattered clothes. He looked up and said, "Damn you for being late! My black cousins were here, playing ball, singing, and drinking.
paragraphs.zh: 里面，我妻子跪在一位穿着破旧衣服、坐在稻草碎屑上的老黑人面前。那老黑人抬起头来，怒道：“你这鬼东西怎么才来！我的黑皮肤亲戚们早就到了，正在这儿踢球、唱歌、喝酒呢。”

paragraphs.en: Each had his own girlfriend except me, who refused to drink because you weren't there."
paragraphs.zh: 除了我不喝，因为你们都有自己的女朋友了。

paragraphs.en: My wife replied, "O my lord and lover, I am married to a cousin who finds me loathsome. If it weren't for you, I would have destroyed his city, now a home for bears and foxes where owls hoot and crows crow." He retorted, "Damn you, liar!
paragraphs.zh: 我的妻子回答说：“哦，我的君主和爱人，我嫁给了一个表亲，他对我极为厌恶。要不是因为你，我已经摧毁了他的城市，如今那里成了熊和狐狸的家园，猫头鹰啼叫，乌鸦聒噪。”他反驳道：“你这个骗子，去你的！”

paragraphs.en: By black chivalry, if my cousins visit tonight and you are not there, I will never befriend or touch you. You cursed woman, you've toyed with me like marble."
paragraphs.zh: 凭着黑骑士的名义，如果我的堂兄弟今晚来访而你不在，我永远不会再与你为友或碰你。你这个该死的女人，你像玩弄大理石一样玩弄过我。

paragraphs.en: When I heard their conversation, the world turned dark before my eyes. My wife cried out, "O my lover, if you remain angry, who else can I turn to? O my lord and light of my eye."
paragraphs.zh: 当我听到他们的对话时，眼前的世界顿时变得一片昏暗。妻子脱口而出：“哦我的爱人，如果你依然生气不原谅我，我又该向谁求助？哦我的君主，我生命中的光明。”

paragraphs.en: She pleaded until he was appeased. Then she removed her outer garments and asked, "My lord, do you have anything for your little girl to eat?" He replied, "Open the copper basin," revealing leftover fried rat bones.
paragraphs.zh: 她央求了很久，直到他才息怒。随后，她脱下了外衣，问道：“lord，你有没有什么给你的小女儿吃的东西？”他回答道：“打开那个铜盆。”只见里面装着一些ngth的油炸鼠骨。

paragraphs.en: After eating them, he gave her some brewed liquor from a jug. She drank it, washed her hands, and lay beside him on reed shavings.
paragraphs.zh: 吃完后，他从壶中倒了些自酿的酒给她。她喝了酒，洗净双手，躺在稻草垫上靠着他。

paragraphs.en: I climbed down from the dome, entered through the door, and took my wife's sword. I struck the black man's neck but thought he was still alive.
paragraphs.zh: 我从穹顶上下来，穿过门进入室内，拿起了妻子的剑。我砍向那个黑人的脖子，但以为他还活着。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what an entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Tomorrow night, if I live, I will tell you something more engaging."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹沉默下来。丁纳扎德说：“姐姐，真是个精彩的故事！”沙赫拉兹答道：“如果我能活到明天晚上，我会给你讲一个更有趣的故事。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister, "Tell us one of your lovely tales." Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达催促妹妹说：“给我们讲一个你那些精彩的故事吧。”沙赫拉扎德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: I heard that the enchanted young man spoke to the king.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说那位被魔法眷顾的青年与国王交谈了。

paragraphs.en: My lord, after striking the black man on the neck and failing to sever his arteries, I retreated and returned to the city. Upon entering the palace, I found my wife mourning her family's losses. She wore a mourning dress and had cut her hair.
paragraphs.zh: 我的 Lord，我在击中那个黑人男子的颈部未能割断他的动脉后退了回来，回到了城里。进入宫殿后，我发现妻子正在哀悼家人的损失，她穿着丧服，头发也已经剪短。

paragraphs.en: She explained that her mother was dead, her father killed in a holy war, and both brothers lost—killed in battle or by a snake bite. I did not reproach her.
paragraphs.zh: 她解释说，母亲已故，父亲在圣战中丧生，两个兄弟也不见踪影——要么死于战场，要么被毒蛇咬伤。我没有责备她。

paragraphs.en: She mourned for a year, weeping daily. Then she requested to build a mausoleum within the palace as a place of sorrow. I agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 她痛哭了整整一年，每日泪流满面。随后请求在宫中修建一座陵墓，作为哀悼之所。我应允了她的请求。

paragraphs.en: She constructed a domed tomb where she placed the wounded black man, who remained silent and only drank liquids. For an entire year, she visited him every day with beverages.
paragraphs.zh: 她为这位受伤的黑人男子建造了一个拱顶墓穴，将他安置在里面。男子始终保持沉默，只喝液体。整整一年，她每天都会带着饮料前来探望。

paragraphs.en: One day, unaware of my presence, she sang:
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，她毫无察觉地唱起了歌：

paragraphs.en: When I see your distress, It pains me, as you see. And when I see you not, It pains me, as you see. O speak to me, my life, My master, talk to me.
paragraphs.zh: 每当见到你陷入困境，我的心也跟着痛，就像你所见的那样。而当你不在时，我也同样感到痛苦，正如你所感知的那样。哦，请对我诉说，我的生命，我的君主，与我说话吧。

paragraphs.en: Then she recited:
paragraphs.zh: 然后她吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: The day I have you is the day I crave; The day you leave me is the day I die. Were I to live in fear of promised death, I'd rather be with you than my life save.
paragraphs.zh: 与你相聚的每一天都是我渴望的日子；你离开我的那一天，对我来说就是死期。如果我因恐死而畏缩不前，倒不如与你在一起，也不愿苟且偷生。

paragraphs.en: After three years of mourning, my wife's persistent grief finally triggered my anger. Upon returning home, I found her in the mausoleum by the tomb, lamenting that she had heard nothing from me for those long years.
paragraphs.zh: 三年的哀痛之后，妻子依旧沉浸在无尽的悲伤中，这终于激起了我的怒火。回到家后，我发现她正独自站在墓碑前的陵园里，叹息着这些年杳无音信的我。

paragraphs.en: She recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 她吟诵着这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: O tomb, O tomb, has he his beauties lost, Or have you lost yourself that radiant look? O tomb, neither a garden nor a star, The sun and moon at once how can you host?
paragraphs.zh: 哦古墓，哦古墓，他的光彩是否消逝？还是你那光辉的容颜已不再？哦古墓，既非花园亦非星辰，如何同时容纳太阳与明月？

paragraphs.en: These verses only fueled my anger. I retorted with my own verses:
paragraphs.zh: 这些诗句反而激起了我的怒火。我针锋相对地回应道：

paragraphs.en: O tomb, O tomb, has he his blackness lost, Or have you lost yourself that filthy look? O tomb, neither a toilet nor a heap of dirt, Charcoal and mud at once how can you host?
paragraphs.zh: 哦墓地，哦墓地，他那阴暗的色彩是否已经消逝？还是你这污秽不堪的模样不再如故？哦墓地，既非厕所也非一堆脏土，炭灰与污泥如何能共存一室？

paragraphs.en: My wife, upon hearing me, leaped to her feet. She accused me of wounding her beloved and tormenting her by depriving him of his youth for three years.
paragraphs.zh: 我的妻子听我这么一说，猛地站了起来。她指控我说伤了她的心上人，三年时间让他失去了青春，这无异于折磨她。

paragraphs.en: I responded with harsh words: "You, the dirtiest whore and filthiest woman who ever desired black slaves, it was I who did this."
paragraphs.zh: 我厉声说道：“你这个最肮脏的妓女，最可恶的女人，竟然想占有黑奴，就是我做的。”

paragraphs.en: With a sword in hand, I prepared to strike. But when she saw my resolve, she laughed and said, "Get away, you dog. Alas, what is done cannot be undone; but God has delivered the one who did this into my hands, setting my heart ablaze with revenge."
paragraphs.zh: 手持利剑，我正准备动手。但她看到我的决心后，却笑道：“滚开，你这条狗。唉，覆水难收；但上帝将施加这一切的人交到了我的手中，让我心中燃起了复仇之火。”

paragraphs.en: She then uttered words I could not understand and cried out: "With my magic and cunning, be half man, half stone." From that moment on, I have been as you see me now—dejected, sad, helpless, and sleepless.
paragraphs.zh: 她随后说出了一串我不懂的话，喊道：“凭我的魔法与机智，你将一半人形一半石像。”从那一刻起，我便成了现在的模样——沮丧、悲伤、无助且彻夜难眠。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister Shahrazad: "Sister, if you are not sleepy, tell us one of your delightful tales to pass the time." Shahrazad agreed with a smile.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达催促她的妹妹沙赫拉兹达：“姐姐，如果你不困的话，给我们讲一个你那些精彩的故事吧，打发时间。”沙赫拉兹达微笑着答应了。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad began: "O King, once there was an enchanted young man who spoke to the king. His wife had transformed him into this state and cast a spell on their city, turning its inhabitants—Muslims, Magians, Christians, and Jews—into fish of different colors. The islands became hills surrounding a lake.
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德说道：“启禀国王，从前有一位被魔法施加的青年向您诉说了他的遭遇。他的妻子将他变成了这种状态，并施咒于他们的城市，使城中的居民——穆斯林、祆教徒、基督徒和犹太人——都化作了不同颜色的鱼儿。而那些岛屿则成了围绕着湖水的丘陵。”

paragraphs.en: Each day, he was stripped naked and whipped until his back bled. Then he was clothed in a hairshirt and luxurious garments."
paragraphs.zh: 每天，他都被剥得赤条条的，鞭打至背部鲜血淋漓。随后，他被穿上一件毛衣和华丽的衣服。

paragraphs.en: The young man wept as he recited: "O Lord, I bear with patience your decree, And so that I may please you, I endure, That for their tyranny and unfair use Our recompense your Paradise may be. You never let the tyrant go, my Lord; Pluck me out of the fire, Almighty God."
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人边念叨着诗句边抽泣：“哦，主啊，我忍耐地承受着你的判决，为了取悦你，我忍受这一切。让我们因暴政和不公而受到的惩罚，得以进入你的天堂。你从不让暴君逍遥法外，全能的上帝，请把我从火中拯救出来。”

paragraphs.en: The king addressed the young man: "You've relieved one burden but added another. Where is your wife and the mausoleum with the wounded black man?" The young man replied, "O King, the black slave lies in a tomb within the mausoleum, in an adjoining room.
paragraphs.zh: 国王对年轻人说：“你卸下了一个负担，却又增加了另一个。你的妻子和那个受伤黑人的墓穴在哪里？”年轻人回答道：“ oh 陛下，那位黑奴躺在陵寝内的一个墓中，在一间相邻的房间里。”

paragraphs.en: My wife visits him at dawn, stripping me naked and lashing me with a whip until I cry out. She then leaves to care for the black man."
paragraphs.zh: 我的妻子黎明时分前来，把我剥得赤条条的，用鞭子抽打我，直到我痛呼出声。随后她便离开，去照料那个黑人了。

paragraphs.en: The king vowed to help the young man: "By God, I will do something that will be remembered." He conversed with the young man until nightfall, then retired.
paragraphs.zh: 国王发誓要帮助这位年轻人：“靠上帝，我一定要做件让人铭记的事。”他与年轻人交谈直到夜幕降临，随后便休息了。

paragraphs.en: At dawn, the king undressed and entered the mausoleum room. Finding it lit by candles and incense-scented, he killed the black man, threw his body into a palace well, and donned the black man's clothes before hiding in the tomb with his sword hidden beneath him.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明时分，国王脱去外衣，走进了陵寝室。只见室内烛光摇曳，香气缭绕，他当即杀死了那个黑人，将他的尸体扔进宫中的水井里，然后穿上那黑人的衣服，藏在墓中，把剑悄悄地放在身下。

paragraphs.en: The witch arrived, stripped naked, and whipped her husband, who pleaded for mercy. She ignored him, saying, "You should have spared my lover."
paragraphs.zh: 女巫赤身裸体地出现了，鞭打着她的丈夫，而丈夫哀求她手下留情。但她置之不理，冷冰冰地说：“你应该放过我的情人。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached. Dinarzad exclaimed, "Sister, what a fascinating story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night to hear more."
paragraphs.zh: 随着晨光渐近，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。丁纳兹阿德脱口而出：“姐姐，这故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答道：“等到明天晚上你就会听到更多。”

paragraphs.en: The king, moved by the young man's plight, decided to postpone his execution for two months, hoping to learn the full tale.
paragraphs.zh: 国王被年轻人的遭遇触动，决定将他的执行日期推迟两个月，希望能听完整个故事。

paragraphs.en: The king mused: "By God, I will spare her and hear the rest of this enchanting story."
paragraphs.zh: 国王沉思道：“天哪，我决定饶了她，听听这个迷人故事的全部。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad told Shahrazad, "Sister, if you are not sleepy, please tell us one of your charming tales to pass the evening." Shahrazad agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达对沙赫拉扎德说：“妹妹，如果你不困，请给我们讲一个动听的故事，打发这个夜晚吧。”沙赫拉扎德应允了。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O King, that after the witch punished her husband by whipping him until he bled and then dressed him in a coarse hairshirt, she went to visit the black man. She entered his mausoleum, cried out, and pleaded with him: "Lover, do not deny me; be generous with your love. Visit me, for my life depends on it."
paragraphs.zh: 我听闻，国王陛下，那位女巫在鞭打她的丈夫直至其流血，并给他穿上粗劣的毛皮衣后，便前往拜访那个黑人。她进入了他的陵墓，大声呼喊并恳求道：“爱人，请不要拒绝我；请慷慨地给予你的爱。来看望我吧，因为我的生命取决于此。”

paragraphs.en: Then she sang:
paragraphs.zh: 然后她唱道：

paragraphs.en: For how long this cruel disdain, Have I not paid enough tears? O lover, talk to me.
paragraphs.zh: 这样的冷酷蔑视我已经忍受多久了？流了多少眼泪还不够吗？爱人，跟我谈谈吧。

paragraphs.en: The king, lowering his voice, stammered and mimicked the black man's accent: "Ah, ah, ah! There is no power but in God." Hearing him speak, the witch screamed with joy and fainted.
paragraphs.zh: 国王压低声音，结结巴巴地模仿那个黑人的口音：“啊，啊，啊！只有上帝才有力量。”听到他这么说，女巫高兴地尖叫了一声，然后晕了过去。

paragraphs.en: When she recovered, she asked if he had spoken to her. The king replied harshly that she did not deserve such treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 恢复过来后，她问他是否跟她说话了。国王冷硬地回答说，她不配受到这样的对待。

paragraphs.en: She questioned why he hadn't helped earlier. He explained that his husband cried all day for help, depriving him of sleep. Only then would he consider speaking to her.
paragraphs.zh: 她质疑他为何没有早点伸出援手。他解释说，他的丈夫一整天都在求救，让他毫无睡眠，只有在这种情况下，他才会考虑跟她说话。

paragraphs.en: She offered to free the man from his suffering but the king insisted on silencing him instead.
paragraphs.zh: 她提出要解救那人脱离痛苦，但国王坚持要让他闭嘴。

paragraphs.en: She left the mausoleum and sprinkled water from a bowl over a young man. She recited a spell, commanding him to stay transformed if cursed or to revert if magically altered. The young man stood up, thanking God for his release.
paragraphs.zh: 她离开了陵墓，用一碗水洒在一位年轻人身上。她念诵起咒语，命令他如果被诅咒就保持变形状态，如果是魔法改变的则恢复原状。那年轻人站起身来，感激地向上帝表示感谢。

paragraphs.en: His wife ordered him to leave permanently.
paragraphs.zh: 他的妻子命令他永远离开。

paragraphs.en: Returning to the mausoleum, she called out to the king, who replied that while her magic had removed his limb, it hadn't freed his body. He explained that every night at midnight, the city's inhabitants and their fish implored God against him. She promised to help them and went to the lake.
paragraphs.zh: 回到陵寝，她喊道国王。国王回应说，虽然她的魔法去掉了他的肢体，但并没有释放他的身躯。他解释说，每晚子时，城中居民和他们的鱼儿都会向上帝祈求摆脱他的控制。她答应帮忙，并前往湖边。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, interrupting Shahrazad’s story. Dinarzad praised the tale, urging her sister to continue. Shahrazad assured Dinarzad that she would share more stories if the king spared her life.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，打断了沙赫拉兹德的故事。丁纳扎德对这个故事赞不绝口，催促妹妹继续讲下去。沙赫拉兹德向丁纳扎德保证，如果国王能饶她一命，她一定会分享更多的故事。

paragraphs.en: The wife spoke over the lake, causing fish to dance. The spell broke, and townspeople resumed their daily activities. She returned to the palace, approached the king in the mausoleum, and urged him to rise.
paragraphs.zh: 湖面上，妻子的话令鱼儿们翩翩起舞。咒语解除后，镇上的居民又恢复了日常的生活。她回到王宫，径直来到陵寝前的国王面前，催促他站起来。

paragraphs.en: He commanded her to come closer, until she touched his body. Then he pushed her away, slicing her with a sword into two halves.
paragraphs.zh: 他命令她靠近一些，直到她的身体触碰到他的。随后，他将她推开，用剑将她从中劈为两半。

paragraphs.en: The king emerged and found the enchanted youth waiting for him. He congratulated the youth on his rescue. The youth kissed his hand, thanked him, and invoked God's blessing.
paragraphs.zh: 国王走了出来，发现那位被施了魔法的年轻人已在等候。他向年轻人成功获救表示祝贺。年轻人吻了吻他的手，道谢，并祈求上帝保佑。

paragraphs.en: The king asked if he wished to stay or join him in his city. The youth replied that their cities were a full year’s journey apart due to enchantment, not half a day as the king thought.
paragraphs.zh: 国王询问青年是否愿意留下，或者跟他一起回到他的城市。青年回答说，由于施了魔法，两座城市之间相距整整一年的路程，并非国王以为的一天半的行程。

paragraphs.en: The king insisted, asking again if the youth wanted to stay or come with him. The youth declared he would never leave the king's side. The king was pleased and said God had given him this son.
paragraphs.zh: 国王坚持问道，询问少年是想留下还是跟他一起走。少年坚决表示绝不会离开国王的身边。国王听了非常高兴，说上天赐给他这样一个儿子。

paragraphs.en: They embraced, feeling happy together. They walked back to the palace where the enchanted young king announced his journey to his kingdom’s leaders and retinue.
paragraphs.zh: 他们相拥而笑，心情愉悦。随后，他们回到了宫殿，那位被魔法眷顾的年轻国王向他的王国领导人和随从们宣布了他的行程。

paragraphs.en: He prepared for a year, packing essential items and gifts from the city's princes and merchants. Departing with fifty Mamluks and numerous guides, he set out with one hundred loads of treasures and money. They traveled day and night for a full year until they reached their destination safely.
paragraphs.zh: 他准备了一整年，打包了必需品和来自城中王子与商人的礼物。带着五十名马穆鲁克士兵和众多向导，他装载了一百担珍宝和钱财出发。他们日夜兼程，整整一年后终于平安抵达目的地。

paragraphs.en: Upon his return, the king sent word to the vizier, who led troops and many townspeople to greet him. Overjoyed at his safe return, the city was adorned with silk carpets. The vizier and soldiers dismounted, kissing the ground before the king.
paragraphs.zh: 国王归来后，派人通知了首相。首相带领着军队和许多市民前来迎接。国王平安归来令全城欣喜若狂，街道上铺满了丝织地毯。首相和士兵们纷纷下马，在地上亲吻以示敬意。

paragraphs.en: They congratulated him and invoked God's blessings.
paragraphs.zh: 他们向他致以祝贺，并祈求上帝保佑。

paragraphs.en: The king returned to his throne after a year's absence. He recounted how he had saved the young man and the city from danger, and the vizier congratulated the young man on his deliverance. The princes, viziers, chamberlains, and deputies then took their places as the king bestowed honors upon them.
paragraphs.zh: 国王在缺席一年后回到了王位上。他讲述了自己如何救下了那位年轻人和整个城市，免受危险。首相向那年轻人表示了祝贺。随后，王子、首相、内臣以及副手各就各位，国王纷纷赐予他们荣誉。

paragraphs.en: He also rewarded the fisherman who had saved both the young man and the city by marrying one of his daughters to the enchanted young man and another to the fisherman himself.
paragraphs.zh: 他还奖赏了那位救下年轻人和全城人的渔夫，将自己的一个女儿许配给这位被施了魔法的年轻人，另一个女儿许配给了渔夫本人。

paragraphs.en: The king then appointed the vizier as ruler of the Black Islands, supplied him with provisions for the journey, and sent fifty Mamluks along with a host of others. He also gave many gifts to all the princes and prominent men there. The fisherman's son was taken into the king’s service, becoming one of his attendants.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，国王任命 vizier 为黑岛的统治者，并为其准备了旅途所需的物资，还派去了五十名马穆鲁克士兵以及众多随从。此外，他还向当地的王子和显要人物赠送了许多礼物。渔夫的儿子也被纳入王宫服务，成为国王身边的一名侍从。

paragraphs.en: The king, the enchanted young man, and the fisherman lived peacefully together. The fisherman became one of the richest men in the land, with his daughters married to kings.
paragraphs.zh: 国王、那位被魔法施咒的年轻人以及渔夫三人和睦相处。渔夫成了国内最富有的人之一，他的女儿们也都嫁给了国王。

paragraphs.en: Morning came for Shahrazad, who fell silent. Dinarzad remarked on the story's wonder and entertainment value. Shahrazad responded that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if the king spared her life.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光来临，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳扎德对故事的奇妙和趣味赞不绝口。沙赫拉兹回应说，这比起她若能保住性命将在第二天讲述的故事来，简直微不足道。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad asked Shahrazad to share a tale. With pleasure, Shahrazad began her narrative.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹德请沙赫拉扎德讲一个故事。沙赫拉扎德欣然应允，开始了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: In the land of Eldoria, King Alaric faced a challenge: to compose a single verse that would enchant his people and restore harmony. He gathered his court poets but found their efforts lacking. Desperate for a solution, he ventured into the enchanted forest, where he met a wise old owl who offered guidance.
paragraphs.zh: 在埃尔多里亚王国，国王阿尔里克面临一个挑战：他必须创作一首能够迷醉国民、恢复和谐的诗篇。他召集了宫廷诗人，却发现他们的努力都未能如愿。为了寻求解决之道，他走进了那片神秘森林，在那里遇到了一位智慧的老猫头鹰，得到了指引。

paragraphs.en: Inspired by nature's beauty, Alaric crafted a verse that resonated with the kingdom. Upon returning, he recited it before the assembled crowd, and the enchantment took hold, bringing peace to Eldoria once more.
paragraphs.zh: 受大自然美景的启发，阿尔里克创作了一首诗句，与整个王国产生了共鸣。回到王宫后，他当众朗诵起来，魔法随之生效，再次为埃尔多里亚带来了和平。
